2. For the reasons stated in the application, the delay in filing instant misc. appeal is hereby condoned.

3. T his miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 17/12/2018 passed by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Vidisha (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 23/2018, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

sentences.text: 5. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Tundaram in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,10,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
6. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellant/claimant has preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.
Learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the appellant at Rs. 6,000/- per month, which is extremely low.
Income of the appellant must be considered as per the Minimum Wages Act.

Despite this, the Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of only Rs.3,10,000/- under all heads,
which is grossly inadequate.
The Claims Tribunal also failed to award just and reasonable amounts under conventional heads such as loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses.
Hence, it is prayed that a just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 3/Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.

8 . Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
9.
On perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimant has utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10651 3 MA-3875-2019 o f Sukhdevi v.
Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways, 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172

sentences.text: Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.7,125/- per month.
10. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, the deceased was 60 years

, therefore,
appellants are not entitled for any future prospects.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 5 has rightly been applied by Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: Also, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131, the claimants are entitled to get compensation towards loss of consortium and loss of estate.

sentences.text: Other Heads:-
Loss of Consortium 40,000X5 Rs. 2,0  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,0

Total Compensation = Rs.5,15,000/-
12.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.
5,15,000/- as against the sum of Rs.3,10,000/- awarded by the learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10651 4 MA-3875-2019 Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs. 2,05,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
13. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs. 2,05,000/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellant in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

14. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
15. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant/claimant stands disposed of accordingly.
